Expiry — the part people forget

Patterns that work in real channels
Daily digest
— a template message (“Top 3 of the day”) with the signature carrying credit; edit the rule weekly, not daily.
Weekly roundup
— Monday 9:00 rule; combine with the calendar to dodge holidays.
Scheduled reminders
— every-6-hours service posts for community managers; Premium's unlimited rules shine here.
Editing and stopping
Rules are editable — change text, time, or pattern, and future instances follow. Pause or delete when a campaign ends. Deleting a rule never deletes already-posted messages.
Why did my recurring rule stop working?

On Free, rules expire after 365 days and you get an expiry notice — create a new rule to continue. Premium rules never expire. Also check the sender bot is still admin — a failed delivery stops the chain.
Can two rules post at the same time?
Yes, and they will — in the order created. If they are too close together, Telegram may throttle the burst; space rules by a few minutes.

Cancelling so you are not charged again

Requests are acknowledged within 7 business days. Once approved, Stars refunds return to your Telegram Stars balance; the total time depends on Telegram, typically a few days.
Can I cancel Premium and keep it until the period ends?
Yes. Cancelling via /premium stops auto-renewal, and Premium stays active until the end of the paid period. Downgrade happens at that boundary, not immediately.
I was charged twice. What do I do?
Email fastschedulebot@gmail.com with both transaction IDs and your Telegram username. Duplicate charges are the clearest refund case and are resolved quickly.
How to Schedule Many Telegram Posts at Once (Bulk Workflow) — Fast Scheduler Help
Scheduling one post at a time is fine for a meme; for a content calendar you want
batch
workflows. Fast Scheduler gives you three, and a full week can be set up in minutes.
Way 1 — import a batch with SetDate
SetDate bot

is the bulk tool: prepare messages as a set (text, times), then import them into Fast Scheduler in one click. It shines when you write copy in advance or migrate from another scheduler. Prepare → import → review in the Message List → done.
Way 2 — let recurring rules do the repeating
Anything that repeats should be a

, not N one-off posts: “every day at 9:00”, “Mondays 18:30”, “every 6 hours”. Premium users get unlimited rules and no expiry; Free has one rule. Combined with a signature, a daily digest literally runs itself.
Way 3 — stock the queue ahead
The queue lets you stack up to 100 pending posts on Free (unlimited on Premium). The classic pattern: one writing session → schedule the whole week → check the
view for holes and collisions → go live your life. Edits are free and instant, so the queue is your draft folder as much as your pipeline.
Checking your work
Three tools keep bulk work honest:
— month at a glance; tap a day to see that day's posts.
— per-channel queue with previews; catch same-time twins here.
— keyword search across everything scheduled, with per-result preview and edit for cleanup.
Is there a true “upload a CSV of posts” feature?
Close: SetDate handles prepared batches, and /import accepts .json/.csv/.txt/.rtf/.odt files of messages. For calendar-scale bulk entry, SetDate is the intended tool.
How far ahead can I schedule?
As far as your queue limit allows — up to 100 pending posts on Free, unlimited on Premium. Times years out are fine.

Why the main bot cannot just post itself
Two reasons, one technical and one yours:
Architecture:

Your brand:
with your own sender bot, posts appear from
bot's name and avatar. Subscribers see your brand, and your bot's admin rights are yours to revoke.

The in-bot wizard walks these exact steps and checks each one, so you cannot get the order wrong.
Security, briefly
Your token is stored encrypted and used only to deliver your posts. You can rotate it any time via @BotFather (
) and update it in the bot — or remove the bot entirely, which deletes the token from Fast Scheduler's storage. If a token leaks, revoke it in BotFather first; a revoked token is dead everywhere.
One bot per channel (Premium: 3×3)

Free pairs 1 sender bot with 1 channel; Premium allows 3 bots across 3 channels. Multiple channels can share one sender bot, but the clean setup — one bot per channel — keeps branding separate and failures isolated.
Can one sender bot serve two channels?
Yes, a sender bot can be paired with multiple channels you own. One bot per channel is still recommended for cleaner branding and simpler troubleshooting.
What happens if I remove the sender bot from the channel?
Scheduling locks (no sender paired for that channel) and queued sends fail until you re-add the bot as admin. The schedules themselves stay saved.
Is my bot token safe with Fast Scheduler?
Tokens are stored encrypted and never displayed in full after saving. Rotating the token in @BotFather instantly invalidates the old one everywhere.

How to Add an Automatic Signature to Every Telegram Post

A signature is the footer that appears under every post in a channel: credit, CTA, hashtags, promo. Set it once in Fast Scheduler and every scheduled message carries it — you stop copy-pasting “@yourchannel” to the end of everything.
Setting it up
via
on the review screen). Premium feature.
2. Pick the channel — signatures are
, so your main channel can carry a promo while the announcements channel stays clean.
3. Send the text. Formatting works:
, links, even emoji-free minimalism if that is your style.
From the next send onward, the signature is appended to every post in that channel. Existing scheduled posts pick it up automatically at send time — no need to reschedule anything.
What belongs in a good signature
The channel handle
— the classic “@yourchannel” line, since forwarded copies keep the credit.
One action
— “Reply to buy”, “Details: link”. A signature with three CTAs has zero.
Hashtags for navigation
— if the channel uses tag-indexing, the signature is the perfect place for the constant ones.
Changing and removing

The same menu edits or clears the signature; clearing stops appending immediately (again, applied at send time, so posts already published keep their footer — that is a feature, not a bug). Per-channel control means experimenting is cheap.
Can I use different signatures for different channels?
Yes — signatures are configured per channel. Each connected channel gets its own text (or none).
Does the signature count toward the message length?
It is part of the final message text, so extremely long signatures can hit Telegram’s 4096-character limit on top of long posts. Short signatures are better anyway.
How Can I See Views, Reactions and Comments on My Telegram Channel Posts? — Fast Scheduler Help
Telegram shows view counts under every channel post, but it never shows you
trends

: which topics overperform, what time of day your audience actually reads, which posts collected the most reactions. Fast Scheduler records the metrics of every post it publishes and turns them into dashboards you can browse in seconds.
Where the numbers live
on the bot’s main menu (page 2) or send
. You get:
Usage totals
— lifetime messages sent, messages sent today, and how many schedules and recurring messages are currently active.
Per-channel dashboards
— for every connected channel: average views, comments and reactions per post, plus the top reactions your audience uses.
Leaderboards (Premium)
— your top posts ranked by the metric you pick: Views, Comments, Reactions or Top Commenters. Each board shows 10 entries per page and can be filtered by period (day, week, month, year or all time).
What is counted — and what is not
Statistics are recorded when
Fast Scheduler publishes a post

and Telegram reports back the post’s metrics. Manually posted content that never passed through the bot is deliberately excluded, so the numbers describe your scheduled content honestly. Comments made in the discussion group under a channel post are picked up too, which is what powers the Comments metric and the Top Commenters board.
Three ways to actually use this
Find your format.
Sort by Views for a month: if the top five posts share a pattern (length, media type, topic), schedule more of it.
Time your channel.
Compare identical formats posted at different hours, then move recurring messages toward the winning window — the best posting times guide below has the general playbook.
Watch reactions, not just views.
Views measure reach; reactions and comments measure resonance. A post with half the views but double the reaction rate is usually the better template.
Does Fast Scheduler track posts I publish manually?
No. Only posts published through Fast Scheduler are recorded, which keeps your dashboards focused on your scheduled content strategy.
Are statistics leaderboards free?
Per-channel averages and usage totals are available to everyone. Leaderboards that rank your top posts by views, comments or reactions are part of Premium.
What metrics can leaderboards rank by?
Views, comments, reactions and top commenters — each filterable by day, week, month, year or all time, with up to 50 posts per page.
Why Was My Scheduled Telegram Post Published at the Wrong Time? — Fast Scheduler Help
When a scheduled message fires at an unexpected hour, the clock itself is almost never wrong — the
used to interpret “9:00” is. Fast Scheduler resolves every time through two settings, and a mismatch between them explains nearly every “wrong time” report.
The two clocks: user time zone and channel time zone
user time zone
— set once via
and used whenever you type a time into the scheduling conversation.
Each channel’s
own time zone
— set per channel, because the audience that reads the channel may live in a different zone than you do. Schedules for that channel are interpreted in the
channel’s
zone.
If your user zone says UTC+3 but the channel zone says UTC+0, a message you schedule for 9:00 is stored as 9:00 channel time — and lands six hours earlier than you visually expected. Check both:
for yourself, and the channel settings inside the bot for the channel.
Daylight saving time

Zones with DST shift by one hour twice a year. Fast Scheduler stores schedules in absolute terms, so a post that crossed a DST boundary can appear to “move” by an hour. If you live in a DST zone and noticed the shift right after the clocks changed, re-check the channel’s zone — picking a zone like
Europe/Berlin
(which follows DST rules) versus a fixed UTC offset produces different results across the year.
Quick diagnosis checklist
Off by a round number of hours
(3, 4, 6…) → time-zone mismatch; fix the channel time zone or your user zone.
Off by exactly one hour
right after late March / late October → DST; confirm the zone uses the right convention.
AM/PM confusion
— schedule with the 24-hour clock (14:00, not 2:00) to remove ambiguity entirely.
Around midnight
— double-check you scheduled the day you meant; the date picker always shows the resolved local date and time for final confirmation before saving.
One more tip: the confirmation screen before saving shows the exact send time. Reading that single line — not the input you typed — is the ground truth for when the post will fire.
Does each Telegram channel have its own time zone in Fast Scheduler?

Yes. Every channel carries its own time zone, and schedules for that channel are interpreted in the channel zone. Your personal /timezone setting applies to how you enter times while chatting with the bot.
How do I change the time zone of a channel?
Open the bot, go to the channel settings, and set its time zone there. Existing scheduled messages keep their stored times, so new schedules pick up the change immediately.
Why Did My Post Go Out at the Wrong Time? Time Zones, Explained Simply
Why Did My Post Go Out at the Wrong Time? Time Zones, Explained Simply — Fast Scheduler Help
“I scheduled 9:00 and it posted at 12:00” — before anything else, check which clock the number 9:00 belongs to. Fast Scheduler schedules posts in a
, and the zone that matters is the one set for the channel, not the one on your watch.
How the bot decides “when 9:00 is”
Every channel has a
time zone setting
. When you schedule 9:00, the bot stores 9:00 in the channel's zone and converts it to UTC behind the scenes.
If the zone is
UTC
(the default) and you are in, say, New York, your 9:00 local is 13:00 or 14:00 UTC — the post will “move” by 4–5 hours from your point of view.
Set the channel's zone to your own city once, and from then on 9:00 means
9:00, every time.
The daylight-saving trap

Zones that observe DST shift twice a year. A post scheduled for 9:00 in March may land at 8:00 or 10:00 relative to the wall clock in November, depending on how the zone handles the shift. If your audience notices a one-hour drift in spring or autumn, that is why. The schedule did not break — the zone's definition of 9:00 changed. Reschedule around the shift week if you post at a strict local hour.
Checking and fixing the zone

, so DST is handled by the same rules your phone uses. Upcoming posts keep their stored times; only
schedules use the new zone, so double-check anything queued for the same day you change it.
Quick diagnosis table
Off by a whole number of hours, constant
— wrong zone set for the channel.
Off by one hour, only in spring/autumn
— DST shift; the zone is working correctly.
Off by a few minutes, growing over weeks
— rare; send
with two examples.
Does changing the time zone move my scheduled posts?
No. Existing posts keep their stored times; the new zone applies to schedules you create afterwards. Verify the next few posts after changing the zone.
What time zone should I pick for an international audience?
Pick the zone of your largest audience segment, or UTC if you think in UTC. Consistency matters more than the specific zone.
What Is Fast Scheduler? The Telegram Post Scheduling Bot Explained — Fast Scheduler Help

(@FastSchedulerBot) is a Telegram bot that plans and publishes posts to your channels on a schedule — the missing native feature Telegram never shipped properly. You write content when inspiration strikes; the bot delivers it at the hour your audience actually reads.
How it works in three roles
The main bot
(@FastSchedulerBot) is your control room: every conversation, every schedule, every statistic happens here.
— connect it once by making the bots admins; the bot verifies rights and tracks it from then on.
A sender bot

Schedule anything

Premium ($6.83/mo or $68.03/yr)

Who it is for

News channels that publish on rhythm, creators who batch their week in one sitting, shops running drops at precise hours, and community managers who share channels with a team. If you have ever set a 3 a.m. alarm to post manually — this bot is the cure.
Start here: open

Is Fast Scheduler free?

Yes — the Free plan runs one channel with 100 pending scheduled messages and 100 sends per channel per month, forever. Premium at $6.83/mo lifts every cap and adds statistics leaderboards, backups and bigger uploads.
Why does Fast Scheduler need a sender bot?
Your sender bot publishes the posts, so your channel’s byline is your own brand instead of a third-party bot. It is created by you in @BotFather and connected in two minutes.
Can Fast Scheduler send messages to a Telegram channel automatically?
Yes. That is its core purpose: scheduled messages publish automatically at their set time through your sender bot, including media, formatting and buttons.
Free vs Premium: Which Fast Scheduler Plan Fits Your Channel? — Fast Scheduler Help
Feature tables tell you
differs; this tells you
when it matters
. Four questions decide the plan.
1. How many channels do you run?

One channel works great on Free (1 channel, 1 sender bot). Two or three channels — or plans to get there — is the cleanest Premium trigger: Premium pairs 3 channels with 3 sender bots from one account.
2. How much do you post?

Multiply daily posts by 30. Under ~90 sends/month, Free's 100-per-channel cap rarely bites. A 3+/day cadence, or channels where every send counts (news, trading, drops), wants Premium's unlimited sends and queue.
3. Is your content video-heavy?

Free uploads top out at 10 MB with video at up to 25MB, no video in Media Storage, and stronger compression. If your posts live on video, Premium's 100 MB uploads, up to 50MB video, and video-in-storage are not a luxury — they are the workflow.
4. Do you need backups, exports or signatures?
The Export & Backup toolkit (
archives, JSON/CSV exports) and auto-signatures are Premium-only. If the queue
your business — client channels, monetized content — backups stop being optional the first time you restructure a month of posts.
The short version
Stay Free
if: one channel, ≤3 posts/day, text-and-photo content, no archive needs.
Go Premium
if: 2–3 channels, 3+ posts/day, video content, recurring automation beyond one rule, or you want backups and signatures.
Either way
: you can start Free and upgrade the moment a limit touches you — nothing you built on Free breaks when Premium ends.
Can I try Premium and go back to Free?
Yes. On expiry, limits revert to Free and nothing is deleted — disconnect extra channels if you keep more than one, and the first recurring rule keeps running.
Does Premium change how fast posts send?
Send speed is the same — Telegram delivery does not differ by plan. Premium removes quantity limits and media compression, not latency.

Here is exactly what happens from click to Premium days, for both sides.
1. Click.
A new user opens your link and starts the bot. The click is recorded instantly, but nothing is granted yet — this is what the "pending" state in your list means.
2. Verify.
The new user connects a channel and schedules at least 1 message — the same verification you completed to unlock the program. Until then, the referral stays pending.

Why Verification Is Required — Fast Scheduler Help
To unlock the Referral Program you must
connect a channel
schedule at least 1 message
. This is not bureaucracy — it is how we verify your account is real.
Why we do it.

Every referral reward is paid out as Premium time, and Premium time costs us real money (Telegram Stars fees and server costs). Without verification, anyone could spin up dozens of empty accounts in minutes and drain the reward pool — which would force us to shut the program down for everyone, including honest users.
What counts as verification.

Connecting a channel proves you have something real to post to; scheduling a message proves you actually use the bot. Both checks are automatic and take most users under two minutes: send your channel link in Step 1 of the tutorial, then schedule any post — even a test message to yourself counts.
What we check — and what we don't.

We only look at anonymous counters (channels connected, messages created). We never read your message contents, never ask for documents or phone numbers, and never share anything with third parties. Verification is purely about activity, not identity.
Common confusion.
Opening the Referral menu before verifying shows a locked screen — that is expected, not a bug. Finish the two steps above and the menu unlocks by itself; nothing else is required.
